stem: Two masses m₁ and m₂ connected by an inextensible cord, m₁ sliding on a frictionless surface and m₂ hanging from a light frictionless pulley. Mass of the falling mass m₂ if m₁ and tension T are known? (a) T/g (b) Tm₁/(gm₁−T) (c) (m₁g−T)/g (d) None —
A smooth wedge has angle θ = 30°. Find acceleration of a block sliding down it. (a) 5.0 (b) 8.7 (c) 3.0 (d) 9.8 m/s² —

Find the speed of block A. (One light string: tied to the top of block A, runs right over a fixed pulley, down round the movable pulley carrying block B, up over a second fixed pulley, left round a pulley attached to A, and right to a fixed wall. Block B moves down with V_B = 12 m/s.)
Find the acceleration of block A (a_A = ?) assuming all surfaces smooth; a_C = 2 m/s², a_B = 1 m/s². —

Figure shows a uniform rod of length 30 cm, mass 3.0 kg. The strings are pulled by constant forces 20 N and 32 N. Find the force exerted by the 20 cm part of the rod on the 10 cm part (in Newton). All surfaces smooth; strings and pulleys light.
If the string is pulled down with a force 120 N as shown (movable-pulley system), then acceleration of the 8 kg block would be. (a) 10 (b) 5 (c) 0 (d) 4 m/s²
v_C equals? Blocks A (5 m/s down) and B (2 m/s down) over a set of pulleys; find v_C. (a) 12 (b) 7 (c) 14 (d) 8 m/s
If masses are released from the position shown, speed of mass m₁ just before it collides on the floor (m₁ > m₂). (a) [2m₁gd/(m₁+m₂)]^½ (b) [2(m₁−m₂)gd/(m₁+m₂)]^½ (c) [2(m₁−m₂)gd/m₁]^½ (d) None
An external force F causes A to move with acceleration a_A. Relation between a_A and a_B equals. (a) 3a_A=4a_B (b) a_A=a_B (c) 5a_A=7a_B (d) 4a_A=3a_A (as printed — an identity in a_A alone)

Velocity of the 'm' mass block equals? (system of nested pulleys, 10 m/s input, block 10m). (a) 10 (b) 30 (c) 70 (d) 60 m/s

The ratio of tensions in the string connected to the block of mass m₂ in figure-(a) and figure-(b) respectively is (friction is absent everywhere) [m₁ = 50 kg, m₂ = 80 kg and F = 1000 N; take g = 10 m/s²]. In (a) F pulls m₁ horizontally along the floor and m₁'s string passes round a pulley on the floor, up over a ceiling pulley, down to m₂. In (b) F pulls the free end of a string that passes round the floor pulley up to m₁, and m₁ is tied by a string over the ceiling pulley to m₂. (a) 7:2 (b) 2:7 (c) 3:4 (d) 4:3

Two small spheres of mass m connected by a string of length 2l are kept on a smooth surface. A vertical force F is applied at the middle of the string. What is the maximum value of F for which the spheres do not lose contact with the surface? (a) 2mg (b) mg (c) 3mg/2 (d) 4mg

Two blocks 'A' and 'B' of mass 'm' and '4m' are connected with a rod PQ of length 'l' and mass 6m through light strings. There is no friction anywhere. End P of the rod slides on the incline (its string runs up along the incline over a pulley to A) and end Q slides on the horizontal floor (its string runs horizontally over a pulley to B). If the system is released from rest and the rod PQ slides on the incline, then for the position shown in the figure (β = angle between rod and incline at P, α = angle between rod and floor at Q), the ratio of the speeds of the mass 'A' to that of the mass 'B' is (a) sinα/sinβ (b) cosα/cosβ (c) cos(α+β)/cos(α−β) (d) sin(α+β)/sin(α−β)
Acceleration of point B at the instant shown (rod remains in contact with wall and floor), given a_A = 3 m/s², angle 37°. (a) 3 (b) 5 (c) 4 (d) 7 m/s²
Acceleration of the block is given by (two-pulley system with m₁, m₂ on a 60° incline). (a) 5a/2 up the incline (b) 5a down the incline (c) 2a/3 down the incline (d) None
Calculate the acceleration of block B (blocks 2m and 4m, force F, pulleys P₁ and P₂; surfaces, pulleys and string all smooth/light). (a) 3F/12 (b) 2F/17m (c) 3F/15m (d) 3F/17m m/s²

Block A (2m) and block B (4m) rest on a smooth floor; F pulls A to the left. One light string is tied to B, runs left round pulley P (attached to A), back right round pulley P₂ (attached to B) and then left to block C of mass m, which also rests on the smooth floor (in the previous question this end was tied to a fixed support). All surfaces smooth, pulleys and string light. Find the acceleration of block B. (a) a_B = 3F/(20m) m/s² (b) a_B = 3F/(21m) m/s² (c) a_B = 2F/(21m) m/s² (d) a_B = 3F/(18m) m/s²
Find force (in N) which mass A exerts on mass B if B is moving towards right with 3 m/s² (all surfaces smooth); also find mass of A. (wedge 37°, B = 1 kg)

In the system shown (all surfaces smooth), the rod is moved by an external agent with acceleration 9 m/s² vertically downwards. Force exerted on the rod by the wedge (37°, 10 kg) will be. (a) 120 (b) 200 (c) 160 (d) 180 N
Find the value of a₂₀ and a₁₀ (blocks 20 kg and 10 kg linked by a nest of pulleys; 500 N applied). (a) a₂₀=8, a₁₀=6.4 (b) a₂₀=10, a₁₀=8 (c) a₂₀=15.15, a₁₀=12.12 (d) a₂₀=12.12, a₁₀=9.69 m/s²
